config.title: Theme Context

intro.title: Theme Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that allows users to toggle between light and dark themes. You will learn how to use React's Context API to manage and share theme state across multiple components without prop drilling. The main technologies involved are React, JavaScript, and JSX, focusing on creating a context, a provider, and a custom hook. By the end, you'll understand how to implement a global theme that updates the UI dynamically based on user interaction.
intro.usecase: Theme Context is a foundational pattern for building consistent, user-customizable interfaces in real-world applications. Developers use it to implement dark/light mode toggles across entire dashboards, like in analytics tools or admin panels, ensuring all components—charts, tables, menus—reflect the user's preference without prop drilling. It's also essential for theming branded products, such as applying a company's color scheme to forms, modals, and buttons globally, enhancing both user experience and maintainability.

objectives: Initialize a React Context for theme management
Construct a ThemeProvider component to wrap your application
Implement a custom hook to consume the theme context
Apply the theme context to style components dynamically
Configure multiple theme values (light and dark) within the context
Update the theme state using a context-provided function
Bind theme values to component styles using the context consumer

steps.title: Import React, createContext, and useContext
steps.instruction: Import React, createContext, and useContext from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all three from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple items from a package
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

steps.title: Create a ThemeContext using createContext
steps.instruction: Create a ThemeContext variable using React.createContext() and export it as a named export.
steps.hint: Use the createContext function you imported to create a new context object. Assign it to a variable called ThemeContext, then export it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeContext object is created and exported, ready to be used as a context provider and consumer.
successCriteria: ThemeContext is created with React.createContext() and exported as a named export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using createContext to create the context and exporting it with the name ThemeContext.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a context using React.createContext() and export it as ThemeContext.

steps.title: Create a ThemeProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ThemeProvider that accepts children as props and returns them wrapped in a div.
steps.hint:
Define a function or arrow function called ThemeProvider that takes a parameter named children and returns
{children}
.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a ThemeProvider component that wraps children in a div.
successCriteria: A ThemeProvider component is defined, accepts children as a prop, and returns children wrapped in a div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your ThemeProvider component accepts children as a prop and returns them inside a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeProvider component is not correctly defined. It should be a function that takes children and returns them wrapped in a div.

steps.title: Initialize theme state in ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside your ThemeProvider component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'theme' initialized to 'light'.
steps.hint: Add useState to the component's body. Remember to import useState if you haven't already.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component now has a 'theme' state variable initialized to 'light'.
successCriteria: ThemeProvider uses useState to declare a 'theme' state variable with initial value 'light'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the correct variable name and initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: use useState inside ThemeProvider to create a 'theme' state variable initialized to 'light'.

steps.title: Create toggleTheme handler in ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, define a function named toggleTheme that switches the theme state between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.hint: The toggleTheme function should update the theme state using the setTheme function from useState. It can check the current theme value and set it to the opposite.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component will contain a toggleTheme function that can switch the theme state.
successCriteria: A toggleTheme function is defined inside ThemeProvider that toggles between 'light' and 'dark' theme values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure toggleTheme is defined inside ThemeProvider and properly toggles between 'light' and 'dark' values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme function isn't quite right. It should be defined inside ThemeProvider and switch the theme state between 'light' and 'dark'.

steps.title: Provide theme data through ThemeContext.Provider
steps.instruction: In your ThemeProvider component, pass the theme state and toggleTheme function as the value prop to ThemeContext.Provider.
steps.hint: The value prop should be an object containing both the current theme and the toggleTheme function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component will now provide both the current theme and a way to toggle it to all child components via context.
successCriteria: ThemeContext.Provider's value prop contains an object with both the theme state and toggleTheme function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the value prop includes both the theme state and the toggleTheme function as an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeContext.Provider needs to receive the theme state and toggleTheme function through its value prop. Check that you're passing them as an object.

steps.title: Wrap the app with ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: In the main App component, wrap the existing content with the ThemeProvider component you created.
steps.hint: Place the ThemeProvider component around the content you want to have access to the theme context.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns content wrapped inside ThemeProvider, making the theme context available to all child components.
successCriteria: App component returns ThemeProvider wrapping the content
ThemeProvider is used as a wrapper component
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure ThemeProvider wraps all the content inside the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the ThemeProvider component to wrap the content in the App component's return statement.

steps.title: Consume theme context in ThemedButton
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemedButton component, use useContext(ThemeContext) to get theme and toggleTheme from the context.
steps.hint: Call useContext with ThemeContext as the argument to access the value provided by ThemeProvider.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemedButton component will have access to the theme context values, preparing it to use them in the next step.
successCriteria: The ThemedButton component uses useContext(ThemeContext) to get theme and toggleTheme.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling useContext with ThemeContext as the argument to get the context value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemedButton component doesn't seem to be consuming the theme context yet. Use useContext(ThemeContext) to access the context values.

steps.title: Style ThemedButton based on theme and wire toggle
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemedButton component, add inline styles to the button based on the current theme value and connect the onClick handler to toggleTheme.
steps.hint: Use the theme value from context to set backgroundColor and color styles. The onClick handler should call toggleTheme.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will have dynamic styling that changes with the theme and will toggle the theme when clicked.
successCriteria: The button has inline styles using theme from context and an onClick handler calling toggleTheme.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the theme value for styling and wiring onClick to toggleTheme.
